real_seq_pub.what: the real private burn on seq-pub (block 6588, dev mode off), P = 6583, T = 6593, witness of vault v4; the journal equals the native statement

bench_guest.what: measurement guest guests/burn_chain_bench (chain check, parse, finder; no note recomputation), executor only; blocks read from copies of the stopped seq-dev and seq-real stores

trust.proven_by_a_proof_of_it: the burn transaction for this note is transaction i of the block with hash H_N; the block does not list it as reverted; its bytes show the bridge program delivering Append{instance, token, denom, note} to the instance's accumulator (private burn), or a holder's Burn root call to the bridge with a config whose instance is this one (public burn); and blocks P..N..T are one unbroken hash chain with rising ids from the pinned (P, hash)
trust.attested: that the hash of block T is on the real, final LEZ chain (one input; today our key, after a delay)
trust.not_proven_still_trusted: that LEZ executed those blocks correctly (rc3 headers carry no state root and public execution is unproven, so 'not reverted' and 'the bridge program sent it' rest on the sequencer having run and verified the transaction), finality, and which chain is the real one (anyone can build a hash chain from the pinned block; the pinned block names the chain, it does not stop a dishonest attester)
trust.gap: the public-burn route is tested only on a synthetic block (fixtures/lez-chain/synthetic/2590): no public burn exists on any chain we run
